newsitem.title: JAPAN: SPEED SKATING-KOREAN TEENAGER TAKES SHORT TRACK TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-KOREAN TEENAGER TAKES SHORT TRACK TITLE.

text.p: Korean teenager Kim Dong-sung unseated reigning champion Marc Gagnon of Canada for the men's overall title at the world short track speed skating championships on Sunday.
But he was then accused of using illegal tactics to achieve the surprise win.

With a slim two-point lead over Gagnon entering the 3,000 metres, the final individual event of the three-day championships, the 17-year-old stayed tucked behind the leaders for most of the race while teammate Lee Jun-hwan set the pace.

Kim took a late lead to finish in five minutes, 14.057 seconds and take the title. Gagnon, world champion in three of the past four years, could only come third in the race which gave him a second place overall.
"The Koreans knew that in order for me to win (the title), I had to win that race," said Gagnon. "(Kim) just followed me the whole race and the other Korean led.
"If he just won on his own, that's all right but if they planned it, I don't think it's fair."
"It's like me skating against the Korean team," he added. "It's an individual sport and we try to win by ourselves."
Kim denied any collusion, saying his teammate had taken the lead without any instructions from their coach and officials also brushed it aside.
"I'm not so sure we can say it was deliberate," said International Skating Union council member Lars-Olof Eklund.
It was a tough day for Gagnon, who earlier saw his overall lead evaporate after a disqualification for cross-tracking wiped out his win in the 1,000 metres.

Kim, the first skater since American Eric Heiden to win junior and senior titles in the same year, moved up to first place to vault into the overall lead. Earlier he finished second in the 500 metres after being disqualified in the opening 1,500 metres.
In the women's event, Chun Lee-kyung of South Korea earned her third consecutive world crown, tying with Yang Yang who became China's first world short track champion.
Korea finished the day by beating Canada in the men's relay. The result was reversed in the women's event.
Chun and Yang split Sunday's races, with Yang triumphing in the 1,000 metres and Chun taking the 3,000 metres.
